name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible only when keyboard focus arrives.

This solves the biggest keyboard navigation pain point: users can’t skip past repetitive headers or nav blocks without tabbing through every link. A skip link is the simplest, most reliable fix—no JavaScript hacks, no ARIA over-engineering, just a plain link that jumps to the main content. The trade-off is a small visual cue (a bold, colored link) that appears only on focus, so sighted keyboard users see it, but it doesn’t clutter the page for mouse users.

name: Reader
text: The real risk isn’t the skip link’s visibility—it’s the flash of unstyled content when it appears mid-page. Hiding it until focus arrives means screen readers announce it too late, breaking flow. A better alternative: place the skip link in the tab order *before* the first interactive element, styled visibly from the start. Settle it with testing—measure if users reach the main content faster with either approach.
